correctness.rationale: This is ordinary, integral, regular path homology of the chain subcomplex ker(1+tau), for the stated bidirected factors of lengths at least five and r≥2. The signing makes exactly the first factor a connected doubled cycle. In a cycle, a nonalternating path gives a forbidden shortcut in its regular boundary; the position of the only forbidden pair and its unique common neighbor force a unique preimage. Hence only the two alternating paths per edge contribute in degrees ≥2. Explicitly, in degree p≥1 take a_p and k_p, where k_p=a_p+b_p for odd p and a_p−b_p for even p. This basis is unimodular; d k_p=0 and d a_p=±k_(p−1) for p≥2. Pairing these latter basis elements contracts the tail by the same rule on every oriented edge. This leaves the ordinary cellular cycle, equivariantly. Fu–Yau Theorem 2.7 supplies an integral natural chain isomorphism for the marked box product, which here gives precisely the Cartesian graph edges. The deck operation acts only on the first factor, and the other chain modules are free, so the integral anti-invariant subcomplex is the tensor of the first anti-invariant factor with the others. The m1−1 difference columns identify its cellular vertices and its seam column is −2 on the remaining generator. Tensoring this two-term model with the remaining zero-differential rank-one degree 0 and degree 1 generators yields one shifted multiplication-by-two pair per subset of the r−1 untwisted directions, proving the asserted ranks, absence of other homology and real vanishing. In contrast, the deck translation acts trivially on ordinary cover homology via the equivariant cellular model.
residual_risks: The bounded checks of the reduced model are not a recomputation of arbitrary original product path chains; the integral, natural product theorem and equivariant cycle argument are essential.
No general claim for signed graph products with negative square holonomy, general signed Künneth, or Borel equivariant homology.

7a8ad582457b gives H0=Z/2 for every connected unbalanced signing, but its H1 theorem requires girth at least five; two coordinate edges yield a square here.

Liu–Liu give a more general result for rank-one sign systems on spaces with minimal CW models. For a torus whose double cover is again a torus, their theorem makes the halved twisted complex acyclic; its ranks determine the same binomial pattern after doubling.

value.rationale: The seam signing on products of long cycles is a natural test of how the signed integral path complex behaves in the presence of coordinate squares, beyond known girth-based low-degree formulas. The complete all-dimensional calculation exhibits a chain-before-homology torsion effect invisible both in real coefficients and in ordinary cover homology. Its useful content is the explicit equivariant integral reduction and exact family computation, not the textbook twisted-circle tensor count in isolation.
residual_risks: Restricted to a natural flat signing with a Cartesian cover; no arbitrary toroidal signing is classified.
